action_label_encoding: JSON labels: {"action":N} for ACTION1-5 (1=up,2=down,3=left,4=right moves of the selected sprite in 3px steps; 5=rotate-or-cycle-variant); {"action":6,"data":{"x":col,"y":row}} selects the sprite whose rendered pixels contain the click. First 63 labels = the banked L1-L3 line from results/arc_loop_solve_cn04.json.
novel_mechanics_found: cn04 is a marker-pair alignment puzzle that escalates from rigid rotations to VARIANT-CYCLING shape grammars. Core loop (consistent L4-L6): ACTION6-click on a sprite body selects it (selected renders in a distinct color WITH its 8-colored 3x3 markers visible; unselected sprites hide markers and render color-4); ACTION1-4 translate the selected sprite in 3px steps; the level completes the INSTANT every 8-marker on every sprite coincides with exactly one 8-marker from another sprite (paired markers render GREEN color-3, live feedback). L4: four rigid sprites, ACTION5 = 90-degree rotation, solved analytically as a 4-cycle chain of marker-offset vectors summing to zero. L5 introduced VARIANT CYCLING: ACTION5 no longer rotates - each sprite cycles through a form catalog: the zigzag PING-PONGS through snake lengths 3-7 markers (a black 0-colored 3x3 head marks the growth tip and vanishes at max length); the E-glyph cycles 2-marker horizontal / 3-marker vertical / 2-marker horizontal / ZERO-marker forms; the C-glyph similarly includes an EMPTY form. Solved by exhaustively cataloging each sprite form then constraint-solving: the unique feasible config was snake-at-max-7 with the other three sprites covering all seven markers 1:1. L6 (recon only): five sprites including a marker-arm that STRETCHES 3px per press (ping-pong) and a snake that GROWS along a winding path 2-to-6 markers with a wandering head - the variant grammar is per-sprite and must be mapped empirically. The top 32px bar ticks on selections/rotations/blocked-moves (not plain moves) and partially REGENERATED when pairs re-formed; it never hit zero so its penalty is unknown.
gotchas: Selected sprite shows markers (8s) and pairs show green (3); unselected sprites hide everything as color-4 bodies - survey by clicking each sprite before solving.

ACTION6 must hit non-transparent rendered sprite pixels; misses are no-ops that may tick the top bar. With overlapping sprites, pick pixels unique to the target (a mis-click selected the wrong sprite once and 11 moves dragged it away - fully recoverable by moving it back, pairs re-form automatically).

ACTION5 semantics are PER-SPRITE and PER-LEVEL: rigid 90-degree rotation on L4; variant-form cycling on L5+ (ping-pong through a form catalog, including ZERO-marker empty forms and length-growing snakes). Map each sprite cycle empirically (4-8 presses, positions of 8s and the 0 head).
The black 0-marker is the snake growth head, not a pairable marker; it vanishes at max length.

Solve analytically offline: catalog marker constellations per form, then constraint-solve (cover + cross-pair with per-sprite consistent translations, all on the 3px grid). The L5 catalog search had exactly ONE feasible configuration.
Sprite bodies may overlap freely; only marker coincidence matters.
Movement clamps at board edges (blocked moves waste an action and tick the bar).
The win fires instantly on the completing move - no validate action needed.

A transient all-green state on L5 did NOT fire the win once (subtle mis-pairing suspected after an accidental sprite displacement); rebuilding the identical config from scratch fired immediately - if all looks green with no win, tear one sprite away and re-place it.

L6 handoff: five sprites - G-hook (3 markers), n-shape (2, offset (3,6)), winding snake (2-6 markers, growth path down-then-right, head wanders), tall bar (2, offset (15,3)), arm-stretcher (3 markers, second marker slides cols 42-51 in 3px ping-pong steps). Rigid current-form pairing is INFEASIBLE - the solution requires specific variant choices; map all five catalogs first (~25 presses).
narrative: Replayed the banked 63-action L1-L3 line, then solved L4 (41 actions) by treating it as vector algebra: four sprites marker-offset vectors form a closed 4-cycle, executed as rotate-measure-translate per sprite with live green-pair feedback confirming each placement. L5 broke the rotation assumption - ACTION5 turned out to cycle SHAPE VARIANTS (snake lengths with a growth-head, forms with zero markers); after cataloging every sprite form empirically, an exhaustive constraint solve found the unique feasible configuration (snake at max length 7, all seven markers covered 1:1), which fired the win instantly once rebuilt cleanly. Gate-verified the 219-action from-reset sequence: reached_level=5, reproduced=True. L6 adds a fifth sprite and richer growth grammars (stretching arms, winding snakes); rigid pairing is provably infeasible and full cycle-mapping plus a second 260+-step gate would not fit the remaining budget, so I banked the verified +2 and documented the L6 recon.
